title: WS-OBLIGATION-CLEANUP Phase 0 — read-only audit findings
author: Mira (Compliance / RegTech engineer, obligations-register curator)
note: READ-ONLY audit. No edits made to _obligations.seed.json or _obligations-register.md. This findings set is the contract the Phase-1 remediation run consumes.

headlineDefects: ORG-PR-30/-35/-53 — three records of the same D1/2015 recovery-plan obligation (fragmentation).
ORG-PA-049 ↔ ORG-PR-66 — same PA Directive D7/2020 SA-CCR leverage obligation, two rows (true duplicate).
15 ORG-PR* [TBD] URNs carry an enumerable SA provision and are mintable now.
ORG-PR(IV)-* (POPIA, 18 rows) nested under the PR prudential ID-scheme but are privacy/data-protection (domain F-as-filed) — ID-scheme/domain incoherence.
honestDeferrals: 13 ORG-PR* [TBD] URNs cite only internal RAS or BCBS-framework text with no enumerable SA provision — deferral is the chosen policy, do not fabricate.
54 TBC citations: the bulk (FX-FIN, MK, PR recovery/resolution) are OCR-gated (GAP-SARB-PDF-OCR, image-only SARB PDFs) or counsel-gated at the licence-application gate.
~157 of the 185 [TBD] URNs are deferred-by-design (IFRS, King IV, internal policy, bare-Act-name HR family) — no enumerable provision exists.

reconciliationToGroundedFacts.tbcCitations: 53 measured vs grounded fact 54 — divergence of 1. By-family measured: PR=23 (fact said 24), FX=14, MK=7, BNK=5, FC=2, GRP=1, EXCON=1. The 1-row drift is in the PR family; likely one PR row resolved its TBC since the grounded snapshot. Flagged for Phase-1 re-count, not a blocker.
reconciliationToGroundedFacts.equivalencePairs: 21 unclassified pairs confirmed; all 21 already carry proposed verdicts in scripts/author-obligation-equivalence-verdicts.ts.

findings.proposedAction: Re-key the POPIA/PAIA privacy obligations off the PR (prudential) ID-scheme. They are data-protection obligations (Information Officer, lawful processing, DSAR, cross-border transfer, PAIA manual) and should sit under a privacy ID-scheme (e.g. ORG-PRIV-* or ORG-PI-*) consistent with deriveDomainLetter, which has no PR(IV) case and would default these to domain J. They are currently filed domain F. Either way the PR-prefix overloads the prudential family. Re-key in Phase 1 with replay-safe ObligationAdopted re-issue; do not break existing citation edges (linkage-safe approach: keep provision URNs, re-mint the obligation id).
findings.reason: Heterogeneous ID-scheme: 18 privacy obligations nested inside the prudential PR family. deriveDomainLetter(platform/regulatory/obligation-linker.ts) has no PR(IV) branch, so these fall to the default domain bucket — a grouping break, not just cosmetic.

obligationIds: __section__:Domain M — OTC Derivative Provider (FMA / FSCA / Joint Standards)
findings.proposedAction: Two register section-headers each span more than one domain letter (Domain M rows carry domain D, C and J; Domain O rows carry E, B and F). Reconcile the section-header to a single domain, or split the section so each row's `domain` field agrees with its section header. Phase 1: assert section→domain is a function (1:1) via a new recon check.
findings.reason: Grouping incoherence: a section header is meant to be a single domain grouping, but rows under these two headers carry up to three different domain letters. Section-vs-domain disagreement defeats per-domain coverage rollups.

findings.proposedAction: No action. Retain the -CONS suffix scheme for consolidated-basis meta-obligations.
findings.reason: The ORG-*-CONS scheme deliberately distinguishes solo-basis obligations (ORG-PR-13 ICAAP) from their consolidated-basis counterpart (ORG-BNK-ICAAP-CONS, group perimeter). This is legitimate scope decomposition, not an ID-scheme defect.

findings.proposedAction: No action on the PA/PR domain split itself. PA-family (150 rows, directive-sourced) and PR-family (164 rows, framework/RAS-sourced) legitimately co-occupy domains A & F because they cite different source layers for related subject-matter. Textual overlap across the two families is low (single strong candidate: ORG-PA-049/ORG-PR-66, captured under duplication-fragmentation).
findings.reason: PA vs PR domain assignment in Domains A & F is correct: the two families are complementary source layers (SARB PA directives vs Basel/RAS frameworks), not a mis-grouping. Verified by pairwise requirement-text comparison — only one true cross-family duplicate exists.

findings.proposedAction: Mint URNs in Phase 1 — each carries an enumerable SA provision. Proposed mints: ORG-PR(IV)-16/-17 → urn:reg:za:paia-2-2000:s51 / :requests; ORG-PR-02 → urn:reg:za:regs-relating-to-banks:reg38 (Pillar-2A); ORG-PR-06/-07 → urn:reg:za:regs-relating-to-banks:reg26 (LCR/NSFR); ORG-PR-12/-13/-14 → urn:reg:za:banks-act-94-1990 family (stress-testing / ICAAP / ILAAP); ORG-PR-22 → urn:reg:za:pa-guidance-note:gn1-2024; ORG-PR-24/-25 → urn:reg:za:regs-relating-to-banks:reg39 (op-risk / NPA). Reuse obligation-linker.normaliseCitationToSectionId + urn.ts schemas to derive the section; honour the no-fabrication rule (if the section number is not extractable, route to the deferred set, do not invent it).
findings.reason: These 15 PR-family rows carry urn:'[TBD]' yet their citation already names a concrete SA instrument + section (Reg 26/38/39, PAIA s.51, Banks Act, PA Guidance Note). The provision exists and is mintable; leaving it [TBD] is a source-referencing gap, not an honest deferral.

findings.proposedAction: Keep [TBD] / route to documented URN_TBD_ALLOWLIST. These cite only internal RAS/RAF (PR-04/-10/-20/-21) or a BCBS framework with no enumerable SA section (PR-08 BCBS 248, PR-11 BCBS d368, PR-15 BCBS 144, PR-16/-17/-18/-26 BCBS op-risk/resilience). No enumerable SA provision exists to mint against. Do NOT fabricate a provision — honest deferral is the chosen policy.
findings.reason: These 11 of the 28 PR-family [TBD] rows have no citable SA provision (internal-policy or Basel-framework-only source). Deferral is correct.

findings.proposedAction: Keep TBC. These TBC citations are gated on (a) GAP-SARB-PDF-OCR — the backing SARB directive PDFs are image-only scans (e.g. D1/2015 recovery plan, 4-page scanned doc) so precise § references are not extractable from repo source docs; or (b) external-counsel ratification at the licence-application gate. findings.reason: OCR/counsel-gated. The TBC marker correctly records that the precise section cannot be cited from current repo source docs. Not a defect — a tracked, reasoned deferral.

findings.proposedAction: Phase-1 triage each TBC against the GAP-SARB-PDF-OCR / counsel-gate criteria; resolve any that have since gained an extractable provision (the PR family showed a 1-row TBC drift since the grounded snapshot). Otherwise retain TBC. Do not fabricate.
findings.reason: Remaining TBC rows across PR/FC/BNK/GRP/EXCON families: each is either OCR-gated or counsel-gated. Honest deferral; revisit when the gate clears.

findings.proposedAction: No action. These terse requirement strings ('IT and operational capacity demonstration.', 'Complaints handling.', 'Record-keeping ≥ 5 years; tamper-evident.') are intentional concise summaries, each backed by a populated urn:reg:za:cs-*-2018 URN — not truncation or pollution.
findings.reason: Spot-check confirmed the terse internal-policy/conduct-standard rows are deliberate summaries with valid source URNs; description is correct, just concise.

findings.proposedAction: No action required to the requirement text, but note: ORG-PR-09's citation field carries an inline correction annotation '[correction (Mira, v1.40, D-BA-330-REATTRIBUTION...)]'. This is provenance metadata, not requirement-text pollution. Confirm in Phase 1 that such annotations live in the citation field (acceptable) and have not leaked into the `requirement` field of any row (sweep for '[correction' / '[citation:' markers in requirement text).
findings.reason: Spot-check of requirement text across the debt families found no mis-citation or leftover pollution in the `requirement` field. The only annotation found is a legitimate citation-field provenance note. Description correctness holds; Phase-1 should add a guard sweep to keep it that way.

findings.proposedAction: Consolidate to a single D1/2015 solo-basis recovery-plan obligation. All three cite SARB PA Directive 1 of 2015 (recovery plan minimum requirements) with near-identical requirement text (board-approved recovery plan: trigger indicators, recovery options, resolution information pack). Keep one canonical row (recommend ORG-PR-53, broadest playbook framing), retire ORG-PR-35 as resolved-by-duplicate, and re-scope ORG-PR-30 to the consolidated/group dimension OR fold it into ORG-BNK-RECOVERY-CONS (which already holds the consolidated-basis recovery obligation). Linkage-safe: redirect any policy/edge citations from the retired ids to the survivor before retiring.
findings.reason: Three rows are records of the same obligation. ORG-PR-35 and ORG-PR-53 are near-verbatim (same D1/2015, same board-approved recovery-plan requirement); ORG-PR-30 adds a consolidated-basis clause that ORG-BNK-RECOVERY-CONS already covers. Fragmentation, not legitimate atomic decomposition.

findings.proposedAction: Deduplicate. Both describe the same obligation — calculate the derivative exposure amount for the leverage ratio using SA-CCR (replacing CEM), per SARB PA Directive D7/2020 (Banks Act s.6(6)(a)). ORG-PA-049 carries the correct hard URN (urn:reg:za:banks-act-94-1990:s6.6a+directive:d7-2020); ORG-PR-66 carries only an internal urn:obligation:bank:prudential:* synthetic. Keep ORG-PA-049 (PA-family, properly sourced), retire ORG-PR-66 as resolved-by-duplicate, and redirect any ORG-PR-66 citation edges to ORG-PA-049 first.
findings.reason: True cross-family duplicate (the single jaccard>=0.45 hit in the Domain A/F PA-vs-PR sweep): same Directive D7/2020 SA-CCR leverage obligation expressed twice. The PA-family row is the better-sourced survivor.

findings.proposedAction: No merge. ORG-PR-01 (maintain regulatory-minimum capital adequacy), ORG-PR-03 (hold conservation + countercyclical buffer), and ORG-PR-04 (internal CET1 management buffer +1.5pp above PA minima) are distinct, layered capital obligations (minimum / regulatory buffer / internal buffer). They look related but are legitimate atomic decomposition, evidenced by their separate equivalence-pair verdicts (PR-01↔rbc:20.2 equivalent; PR-01↔rbc:30.2 gold-plates; PR-03↔both).
findings.reason: Related-but-distinct capital obligations. The equivalence-verdict spine treats them as separate nodes; collapsing them would lose the minimum-vs-buffer distinction. Not duplication.

findings.proposedAction: Classify the 21 unclassified SA↔BCBS equivalence pairs using the verdicts already authored in scripts/author-obligation-equivalence-verdicts.ts (one ObligationEquivalenceClassified event per pair). Proposed verdicts (from that script): RBC capital minima (PR-01/PR-03 ↔ rbc:20.2) = equivalent; conservation buffer (PR-01/PR-03 ↔ rbc:30.2) = sa-stricter-gold-plates; CRE pairs (PR-RETURNS-007 ↔ cre:20.8/20.32/22.67) = equivalent; market risk (PR-19 ↔ mar:20.1) = materially-divergent, (PR-19 ↔ mar:33.1/32.18) = equivalent; LCR (PR-06/PR-36 ↔ lcr:20.5/30.43/40.1/40.77) = equivalent; NSFR (PR-07 ↔ nsf:20.2/30.1) = equivalent; large exposures (PR-40 ↔ lex:10.8) = equivalent. Run the one-off author script against the SHARED store (BANK_EVENT_DB=$HOME/.local/share/bank/event.db) in Phase 1; recon:obligation-divergence drives the unclassified count to zero.
findings.reason: 21 SA↔BCBS pairs are unclassified (22 already classified). Each already has a merits-based proposed verdict (priored on the basel-adoption.ts ADOPTION_EDGES adoptionType). Resolvable now — these are not duplicates but unclassified-equivalence gaps; classification is the Phase-1 action.
